welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.subtitle: Real-time deadlift form analysis powered by on-device AI. Create an account to save sessions, or continue as a guest to explore the app.
welcome.featureBody: MoveNet Lightning tracks pose keypoints from the camera for instant form cues on each rep — no extra wearables required.
welcome.step1Body: Place your phone 5–7 feet away with a full-body view from the side.
welcome.step2Body: Execute your set as normal. The AI detects start and end points automatically.
welcome.step3Body: Receive instant feedback on depth, pathing, and tempo.
welcome.infoNote: Guest mode lets you try workouts locally. Sign in to sync progress and unlock full Stats history.
welcome.languageSub: Choose your preferred language for the app.

support.title: Support & contact
support.emailBody: For account help, data requests, or bug reports, email us. We typically respond within a few business days.
support.helpBody: For form analysis tips, place your phone 5–7 feet away with a full side view of your body. Ensure good lighting and keep the barbell in frame. Exercise feedback generated by the app may be inaccurate and should not be relied upon as a substitute for professional coaching or medical advice.
support.researchBody: RepRight is developed at Universidad Iberoamericana (UNIBE) for academic research on exercise form analysis using on-device computer vision.
support.footer: RepRight · UNIBE · Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic

q1.prompt: How should your lower back be while lifting the weight from the floor?

options.a: Straight or in a natural position, without excessive rounding
options.b: Arched backward as much as possible to protect the bones
options.c: Rounded forward to reach the bar better

q2.prompt: What is the main risk of rounding your back during the lift?

options.b: The exercise is less tiring for your legs
options.c: Injury or pain in the spinal discs

q3.prompt: Before you start lifting, where should your hips be?

options.b: Almost touching the floor, like sitting in a low chair
options.c: At a similar level or slightly below your shoulders

q4.prompt: What is the hip hinge movement?

options.a: Push your hips back while keeping your back firm
options.b: Fall forward without moving your legs
options.c: Bend only your knees to lower your body

q5.prompt: Throughout the lift, how close should the bar stay to your legs?

options.a: Far enough not to hit your knees
options.b: As close as possible to your shins and thighs
options.c: About 20 cm away to leave space

q6.prompt: What happens if the bar drifts far from your body as you rise?

options.a: You feel much more load and pressure on your lower back
options.b: The exercise becomes more effective for your arms
options.c: It is easier to balance the weight

q7.prompt: When you are standing with the weight up, what mistake should you avoid?

options.a: Leaning your back far backward (excessive arching)
options.c: Squeezing your glutes at the finish

q8.prompt: At the start position, where should your shoulders be relative to the bar?

options.b: Directly over the bar or slightly in front

q9.prompt: What happens if you start pulling with your hips very high?

options.a: Your leg muscles work more effectively
options.c: The load shifts to your lower back, increasing pain or injury risk

q10.prompt: If your shoulders are far behind the bar at the start, what problem does that cause?

options.a: The exercise feels more comfortable for your arms
options.b: You lose balance and the pull becomes less efficient (harder)
options.c: It helps keep your back straighter
